RUNBRIDGE AI DOCUMENTATION

Your first request

One bridge to every generation model. Start with a familiar SDK and an account-specific endpoint.

This is an integration preview. Live account creation and API credentials are not connected to this site.
AuthenticationKeys & configuration →Request guideText, image & video →Error handlingRetries & timeouts →

Before you start

  • A server-side environment for your chosen language.
  • A provisioned account with its API key and base URL.
  • An exact model version ID and the schema it supports.

1. Prepare your configuration

You will need an API key, a base URL and the exact model ID from your provisioned account. Keep credentials on your server.

RUNBRIDGE_API_KEY=your_account_key
RUNBRIDGE_BASE_URL=your_account_endpoint
RUNBRIDGE_MODEL=your_selected_model_id

2. Choose a client

The examples below use an OpenAI-compatible chat request. Verify the selected model’s supported parameters before sending a live call.

quickstart.pyEXAMPLE
OpenAI-compatible request format{ }
Integration preview. Set RUNBRIDGE_BASE_URL, RUNBRIDGE_API_KEY and RUNBRIDGE_MODEL to your provisioned account values when available.
Choose the correct clientPython and JavaScript examples use the OpenAI SDK in a server environment. The cURL example sends an HTTP request directly.View integration setup →
3. Review the response
Check the returned content and usage fields. Record your request identifier, model version and timing so you can investigate failures and compare runs.
4. Move beyond text
Image and video models have different inputs, settings and output lifecycles. Use the selected model’s documented schema instead of sending every workload to the chat endpoint.
Before your first production request
  • Set a request timeout and a bounded retry policy.
  • Log the model ID and request ID without recording secrets.
  • Review usage fields and confirm the selected model’s billing unit.
  • For job-based APIs, save the job ID before polling for results.
